item.content:encoded:
Supervisor of Elections, Ana Mataiciwa will appear on fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan at 7pm tonight.

The show will focus on the state of preparedness of the Fijian Elections Office for the proposed national referendum on December 9th and the next general elections which has to be held by February 6th 2027, the nationwide voter registration underway, changes to the electoral laws and the impact on the voters and the country, and the impact of any drastic changes with two months to go for the last day for the Writ of Elections to be issued on December 24th 2026 amongst other issues.

You can watch the Straight Talk interview on our facebook page, TikTok, YouTube and Instagram accounts.

You can also check out the podcast, fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan on Spotify and Apple podcasts.

item.title: Tagicakibau calls for social media ban for children aged 16 years and under
item.description: Tailevu resident Leone Tagicakibau is calling for children aged 16 and under to be banned from using social media platforms, including TikTok, to protect them from negative influences and help them become responsible future leaders. While making his submission to the Joint Parliamentary Special Committee on the Constitution Amendment Bill at Rakiraki Hall, Tagicakibau says he is concerned about th
item.content:encoded:
Tailevu resident Leone Tagicakibau is calling for children aged 16 and under to be banned from using social media platforms, including TikTok, to protect them from negative influences and help them become responsible future leaders.

While making his submission to the Joint Parliamentary Special Committee on the Constitution Amendment Bill at Rakiraki Hall, Tagicakibau says he is concerned about the behaviour and vulgar language used by some young people on social media.

He believes children need proper guidance and protection from harmful influences as they grow up.

Tagicakibau says restricting social media access for children aged 16 and under could help prepare them to become responsible leaders in the future.

He also raises concerns about what he sees as a lack of youth representation in national leadership.

Tagicakibau says young people should be given more opportunities to serve on boards and statutory bodies so they can contribute to important decisions affecting the country.

He stresses that young people should not only be regarded as leaders of tomorrow but should also be recognised as leaders of today.

Tagicakibau, who travelled from Nadi to Rakiraki to make his submission, says he wanted to contribute to the constitutional review process as a young leader concerned about Fiji's future.

On other issues raised in his submission, Tagicakibau proposes recognising Christianity as an important part of Fiji's history and national values while respecting freedom of religion and the rights of people from other religious backgrounds.

He says his intention is to preserve Fiji's Christian heritage, while ensuring that everyone can continue to live and worship freely.

Tagicakibau also highlights the importance of recognising Fijian identity and cultural heritage while respecting people of all races who call Fiji home.

item.title: SODELPA seeks clarification on proposed constitutional changes affecting GCC
item.description: The Social Democratic Liberal Party is calling on the Parliamentary Special Select Committee reviewing the Constitution Amendment Bill to clarify how the proposed changes will affect the membership, funding and independence of the Great Council of Chiefs. SODELPA is seeking clarification on Section 152(3), which it says gives Parliament the power to make laws determining the membership of the Grea
item.content:encoded:
The Social Democratic Liberal Party is calling on the Parliamentary Special Select Committee reviewing the Constitution Amendment Bill to clarify how the proposed changes will affect the membership, funding and independence of the Great Council of Chiefs.

SODELPA is seeking clarification on Section 152(3), which it says gives Parliament the power to make laws determining the membership of the Great Council of Chiefs.

The party is questioning whether a government with a simple majority in Parliament, could change the Council's membership requirements without needing to amend the Constitution.

They also wanted to know why the representation of Fiji's 14 provinces, Rotuma and paramount chiefs has not been clearly protected under the proposed amendments.

SODELPA says it is important to ensure that traditional leadership remains independent and protected from political interference, regardless of which government is in power.

The party is also seeking clarification on Section 152(4), which provides for Government funding of the Council, subject to available resources.

They are questioning whether this arrangement provides sufficient financial independence for the Council and why guaranteed funding directly from the Consolidated Fund has not been included.

SODELPA has also raised questions about the protection of iTaukei land, qoliqoli and mineral rights.

It wants clarification on whether the proposed amendments provide adequate safeguards for these rights, particularly in the absence of an express veto power for the Great Council of Chiefs.

Meanwhile, the party says the 30-day public consultation period is insufficient for provincial councils, districts and traditional leaders to fully examine and understand the proposed changes.

They are calling for an extension to allow communities more time to consider the Bill and its possible implications for their rights and traditional leadership.

SODELPA is urging the Parliamentary Special Select Committee to provide clear public explanations on these issues before the Bill progresses.

The party says it will continue to advocate for the protection of the authority and independence of Fiji's chiefs and traditional leaders.

item.title: Police await post-mortem results in Thurston Garden death investigation
item.description: Police say the post-mortem examination of the woman found dead at Thurston Garden on Friday night will be conducted soon, as questions remain about whether police have already checked CCTV footage and spoken to witnesses as part of their initial investigations. Police have confirmed that the investigation is still in its early stages and they will wait for the post-mortem results before proceeding
item.content:encoded:
Police say the post-mortem examination of the woman found dead at Thurston Garden on Friday night will be conducted soon, as questions remain about whether police have already checked CCTV footage and spoken to witnesses as part of their initial investigations.

Police have confirmed that the investigation is still in its early stages and they will wait for the post-mortem results before proceeding further.

The woman’s identity has been confirmed by her family, and the post-mortem examination is expected to help determine how she died.
